mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS over 20-day horizon remains below 0.03 in 70% of 3-year rolling windows, or average 20-day returns during declining FEDFUNDS are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises >0.3pp monthly, 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate contracting consumer demand, triggering reduced corporate revenue expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS (both below 3-month moving average) fails to produce negative 60-day returns in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regime, INDPRO decline does not yield negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening residential investment and consumer confidence, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for HOUST over 5-day horizon remains below 0.03 in 70% of 3-year rolling windows, or average 5-day returns during rising HOUST are not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation that triggers Fed tightening expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises >0.3% monthly, 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates labor market tightening and monetary policy shift, reducing corporate hiring and investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Joint condition of PAYEMS decline and FEDFUNDS rise fails to produce negative 20-day returns in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In demand-driven expansion, a quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) signals recession risk that triggers equity sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In demand-driven expansion regime, GDPC1 decline does not yield negative 5-day returns in >60% of cases, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
